8.1.1: O Suta, the greatness of the incarnations of Siva inclusive of their narratives, has been well explained by you with a desire for the welfare of the world.
8.1.10: O dear, may the excellent grandeur of Siva be narrated with pleasure in connection with his phallic forms. You arc blessed and the most excellent among the devotees of Siva.
8.1.11: Listening from your lotus-like mouth, O holy lord, to the nectar-like glory of Siva, we are never satiated. Let the same sweet narrative be repeated.

8.1.13: O brahmins, O excellent sages, yqu have asked well. 1 shall explain them in brief with a desire for the welfare of the worlds and due to my affection for you.
8.1.14: The holy centres are equipped with phallic images. Everything is founded on these. There is no limit to their number. I shall mention a few of them.
8.1.15: O excellent ones, the three worlds consisting of the gods, Asuras and human beings are pervaded by Siva in the form of phallic image for the welfare of the worlds.
8.1.16: In order to bless the worlds, lord Siva assumes different phallic forms here in the holy centres as well as in other places.
8.1.17: Siva incarnates in those places wherever he is devoutly remembered by the devotees. After carrying out their task he stations himself there.
8.1.18: He has assigned his phallic form for the bene6t of the worlds. The devotee attains perfection by worshipping that form.

8.1.20: He who reads or recites the twelve names early in the morning is freed from all sins and attains the fruits of all Siddhis. The twelve Jyotirlihgas are—Somanitha in Saurastra, Mallikarjuna in Srilaila, MahSka in Ujjayini Paramevara in Orhkira, Kedara on the Himavat, Bhima- Sankara in Dakini, Viivea in Varanasi, Tryambaka on the bank of the Gautami, Vaidyanatha in the cremation ground, Nagea in the Daruka forest, Ramela at Setubandha and Ghumesa at Sivalaya.
8.1.21: O great sages, such excellent men will attain those desires for which they recite the names.
8.1.22: Those who recite them without any desire but with purity of mind will never have rebirth involving residence in the mother's womb.
8.1.23: By worshipping these, people of all castes get their miseries destroyed in this world and become liberated hereafter, to be sure.
8.1.24: The food offerings of these Jyotirlihgas shall be taken and others shall be fed with the same. Such acts reduce the sins to ashes instantaneously.
8.1.25: O brahmins, the results of the worship of Jyotirlihgas cannot be described adequately by Brahmi and others.
8.1.26: Even if a person of base birth happens to see Jyotirlihga, he will be born in a pure and good family.
8.1.27: Being born in a good family he will become rich and master all the Vedas. Then by performing auspicious rites, he shall attain liberation without any obstacle.
8.1.28: O great sages, whoever he may be, an outcaste, a slave or an eunuch, he will be born as a brahmin and become liberated. Hence one shall view the Jyotirlihga.
8.1.29: O excellent sages, a few of the fruits of the Jyotirlihgas have been narrated by me. Let the Upalihgas (ancillary phallic forms) of these Jyotirlihgas be listened to.
8.1.3: O brahmins, thus I have mentioned the Upalihgas and the Jyotirlihgas. They dispel sins by their sight and yield the fruit of all desires.
8.1.30: These are the most important ones. O excellent sages, let the other important ones also be heard.
8.1.31: Srhgelvara as also Vaidyanatha are famous. What is famous as Japyelvara stands at the battle-ground of Dadhici.
8.1.32: Gopelvara, Rahgelvara, Vamcivara, Nagela, Kamesa, Vimalelvara, Vyaselvara, Sukela, Bhandelvara, Huihkarela, Surocana-Bhutelvara and Sahgamela are the des¬ troyers of great sins.

8.1.36: Somevara wards off all adversities. Bharadvaje- vara increases Brahmacarya.

8.1.45: There is a great forest Kamada'*' in the south near Gitrakuta. It is benehcient to the good in the performance of penance. There the son of Brahma, the sage Atri, performed a severe penance accompanied by Anasuya.

8.1.6: On seeing the dissolution of all living beings, the chaste lady, the beloved wife of Atri said to her husband. ''I cannot bear this distress.**
8.1.7: The sage then sat in the yogic pose, repeated the Pranayama three times and sank into the yogic trance.
8.1.8: Atri, the great sage of perfect knowledge, meditated on Siva devoid of aberrations, the great splendour stationed in the soul, through his own soul.

8.2.0: Anasuya the well behaved wife of the sage circumambulated her lord and Siva. After prostration she went round anticlockwise too. On seeing that beautiful lady the Daityas and Danavas were excessively agitated by her brilliance. They kept themselves away as people do from a blazing fire.
8.2.1: O leading brahmins, Anasuya's service to Siva performed sacredly through mind, speech and body surpassed even the penance of Atri.
8.2.10: O excellent sage, the couple thus engaged in their activities remained there, alone.
8.2.11: Thus a long time elapsed. The excellent sage, sunk in great meditation did not wake up at all.
8.2.12: Anasuya the chaste lady worshipped only her lord and Siva. That chaste lady did not care to know anything else.
8.2.13: On account of his penance and her worship the gods and the sages, Gahga and the rivers came there in order to see them with pleasure.
8.2.14: On seeing his penance and her service they were surprised. On seeing their wonderful activity they asked one another. "Which of the two—the penance or the service, is the greater?" They themselves replied—"Arti's penance is good but Anasuya's service is better".
8.2.15: On seeing their performance some said "Her ser¬ vice is better." Others said "Difficult penances had been performed by sages of yore but nothing like Dadhici's penance was ever performed by any".
8.2.16: The sage is blessed. Anasuya is blessed, since great penance is pursued by these with great pleasure. If there be a person performing such an auspicious, difficult and excellent penance anywhere in the three worlds, we do not know.
8.2.17: After praising them thus, they went away but only Gahga and Siva were left.
8.2.18: **Delighted in worshipping us the chaste lady is too much engrossed in virtuous rites. I shall* help her and then go."
8.2.19: O great sages, $iva too, drawn by the meditation of Atri, stationed himself there in full digits. He did not go to Kailasa.
8.2.2: O excellent sages, fifty-four years had elapsed. There was no rain at all.
8.2.20: As long as the sage was in meditation and penance, Anasuya decided not to eat anything. Now listen to what happened when tho- sage was performing penance and Anasuya continued her service.
8.2.21: Once that great sage Atri, the foremost among the knowers of Brahman woke up and spoke to his wife "Give me water."
8.2.22: Of course the chaste lady took the water pot and went into the forest. (But she began to muse) "Whence can I fetch water? What all I do? Where shall I go? How can water be fetched?" Wondering thus she saw Ganga.
8.2.23: By the time she went over to her, Ganga, the most excellent river, assumed a beautiful form and spoke to her. Gahgd said:—
8.2.24: O gentle lady, I am delighted with you. Where are you going? Tell me now. O fortunate lady, you are blessed. I shall truly carry out your behest.
8.2.25: On hearing her words the saintly woman, the wile of the sage, was greatly surprised O brahmins. She replied with great pleasure.
8.2.26: O beautiful lady with eyes like lotus-petals, whence have you come? Please tell me the truth. A chaste lady speaks good words.
8.2.27: O great sages, when the wife of the sage spoke thus, the divine formed Gahga, the foremost of the rivers, said.
8.2.28: O chaste lady, on seeing the service rendered by you unto your lord and to iSiva the great soul and on taking view of your holy rites, I am staying near you.
8.2.29: O lady of pure smiles, I am Gahga come here attracted by your worship. Choose whatever you wish.
8.2.3: On hearing her words Gahga said—"Dig a pit." She then made a pit in a trice, came and stood before her.
8.2.30: Gahga entered the pit which became full of water In surprise, Anasuya took the water.
8.2.31: Anasuya the wife of the sage spoke for the welfare of the people to Gahga, the excellent river of divine form.
8.2.4: If you are delighted, if you have sympathy for me you will please stay here till my husband comes.
8.2.5: On hearing the words of Anasuya pleasing to the good, the delighted Gahga said—''O sinless lady, you will give my water to Atri."
8.2.6: When Gahga said thus, Anasuya acted accordingly. She gave the divine water to her lord and stood before him.
8.2.7: The sage performed the Acamana duly with great pleasure and drank the divine water. On drinking it he derived great happiness.
8.2.8: "O this is not the water usually drunk by me." After thinking thus he suddenly looked all round.
8.2.9: On seeing the trees dry and witherecf and the quarters rough and arid, the excellent sage spoke to her "No rain has fallen?"

8.3.20: Then the sage took a clean bath in that excellent water. After performing the Acamana he eulogised her again and again.
8.3.21: Anasuya too took her bath in that beautiful, clear water. The sage performed the routine rites. Anasuya too, of good rites, performed likewise.

8.4.12: A certain noble brahmin there, born of the family of Utta, entrusted his wife to the care of his two sons and went to Kai.
8.4.13: The brahmin died there itself. On getting the news the two sons performed the obsequies.
8.4.14: The wife looked after the sons, seeking their welfare. After bringing up the sons she divided the assets.
8.4.15: She reserved some amount for her funeral expenses. After sometime when she was'going to die, she made pious gifts of various sorts. O brahmins, providentially she did not die.
8.4.16: When she did not die providentially, the son observing her ailments said.
8.4.17: The elder son replied—"Please do mention. I shall do the same." She then replied.
8.4.18: O son, hear with attention. I had a great desire to go to Kaii. That was not to be. Now I am dying here.
8.4.19: Dear son, my bones shall be cast off into the waters of the Gahga assiduously. That pious act will bless you, to be sure.
8.4.2: When she of good rites and on the verge of death, said thus, the affectionate elder son replied to her.
8.4.20: "O mother, you shall die peacefully and with confidence. I shall carry out youi* task first and then attend to mine."
8.4.21: After saying this, he handed water to her and went to his house. Remembering Siva, she died in the meantime.
8.4.22: After performing her obsequies and the monthly Sraddha he started on his journey.
8.4.23: He engaged a servant to accompany him. He consoled his wife and sons. He performed Sraddha, Dana and other pious rites. He then set out from his houre after Mahgala Smarana accompanied by the servant.
8.4.24: He walked about twelve kilometres that day and when the sun set, he halted at the house of a certain Brahmin in the auspicious village of ViihSatigrama.
8.4.25: He performed Sandhya and other rites duly. He recited the hymns of prayer to Siva of wonderful activities.
8.4.26: The brahmin stayed there accompanied by the servant. The night had passed by two muhurtas when something surprising happened. O sages, listen attentively.
8.4.28: O great sages, on seeing the cow, tethered in the courtyard, not yet milked, the distressed brahmin desirous of milking it told his wife.
8.4.29: In order to milk the cow he called his wife quickly and said *'0 beloved, the cow is not yet milked." Thus urged she brought the calf.
8.4.30: O sages, the owner of the house, the brahmin, desirous of milk tried to tie up the calf to the peg.
8.4.31: Dragged by the leg the calf kicked. O great one of good rites, the brahmin was put to pain.
8.4.32: Infuriated by the kick of the calf, he hit the calf severely with the pieces of firewood.
8.4.33: Hit by him the calf became utterly exhausted. Due to anger neither the cow was milked nor the calf was untied by the brahmin.
8.4.34: For the pleasure of getting milked, the cow mooed loudly. On hearing the mooing sound of the cow, the calf said.
8.4.35: *'0 mother, why do you cry? What is the misery that has befallen you? Please tell me lovingly.** On hear¬ ing this, the cow said.
8.4.36: *'0 son, listen to me. Although I am unable to express my grief adequately, you have been hit by the wicked man. Hence I am distressed.**
8.4.37: On hearing his mother's words, the calf taking his stand by the principle of previous action replied enlightening his mother.
8.4.38: "What should be done? Where should we go? Since the results are bound by previous actions, we experience joy or sorrow accordingly.
8.4.39: Activities are pursued with pleasure and fruits are derived sorrowfully. There is none who gives misery and none who gives happiness.
8.4.4: Misery or happiness results from our own actions. Hence action is prominent and everything is founded on action.
8.4.40: You the mother, I the child and all the Hiring beings are bound by action. They are not to be bewailed by you.
8.4.41: On hearing these words of her calf full of wisdom, the distressed cow sorrowing for her calf, said thus.
8.4.42: '*0 dear son, I know fully well that all the people are subservient to their actions. Still, seized by Maya I feel much distressed.
8.4.43: I have cried a lot but the sorrow has not sub¬ sided.** On hearing these words, the calf spoke to her again.
8.4.44: If you know thus, can anything be gained by crying? Hence leave off your sorrow.
8.4.45: On hearing the words of her son, the distressed cow heaved a deep sigh and spoke to the calf.
8.4.46: My distress will disappear only when a similar misery befalls the brahmin. I am telling you the truth.
8.4.47: Tomorrow morning I shall hit him by my horns. No doubt, when hit he will lose his life.

He used to tell his wife, "No doubt I am a householder. But what can I offer to a guest? If any poor man comes you shall tell him "My husband is not here." It happened once that a guest oppressed by thirst and hunger visited the house. He asked the lady "Where is your husband? Where has he gone?" She replied "My husband is not here." Knowing the truth by his divine vision the sage said, "He is hidden inside the house." The brahmin died in his hiding place. When permitted by his preceptor ViSvarxiitra, the son of the brahmin, Galava returned home and heard from his mother the terrible calamity that had overtaken them. He propitiated lord Siva and performed Siva's worship. When he went out of his house remembering Siva in his heart, he saw his father alive again who on seeing the son standing with palms joined in reverence said—"Thanks to the favour of lord Siva I am blessed and satisfied. 9.3.63: O holy lord, son of Brahma, obeisance be to you. Please describe those living beings who are engaged in sins causing their fall into great hells.
9.3.64: I describe to you in brief the living beings who are engaged in sins that cause their fall into great hells. Listen attentively.
9.3.65: Pondering over other men's wives and wealth, wishing for the ill of others mentally, conception of various evil actions and ardent longing for various mean acts, these arc the four types of mental activity.
9.3.67: Eating forbidden food, violence, wild goose chase and pilfering of other's property, these are the four types of physical activity.
9.3.68: Thus there are twelve types of activity intended to achieve three aims. I shall explain their further sub¬ divisions, the results of which are endless and manifold.
9.3.69: Those who censure the propoundcr of Siva's perfect knowledge, ascetics, preceptors or parents are mad. They fall into the ocean of hell.
9.3.7: The following six are the great sins attended with endless evil results, viz:—censure of Siva, censure of the preceptor, censure of Siva's perfect knowledge, misappropri¬ ation of the wealth of the lord, destruction of the wealth of brahmins and the foolish stealing of the sacred text of Siva's perfect knowledge.
9.3.70: The following too are great sins and those who commit them are great sinners. Those who do not take delight on seeing a well-arranged worship of Siva, who do not bow to or eulogise it on seeing his phallic image that is worshipped, those who do not scrub, clean and sanctify the spot of worship during festival days; those who do not duly cooperate with the preceptor in their sacred rites; those who misbehave as they please, play about mischievously and do not render service in front of Siva or in the presence of the preceptor; those who eschew §aiva course of conduct and discipline, those who hate Siva's devotees; those who begin to study or write about Siva's knowledge without worshipping; those who give without justice or justification; those who listen or recite indiscriminately; those who sport about covetously; tho.se vho pursue false knowledge or do not have proper rules and regulations; those who lie down and sleep in dirty uncleaned spots; he who abuses Siva's story and knowledge and begins to expatiate on other things; he who does not speak the truth; he who does not
9.3.71: The murderer of a brahmin, the addict to wine, the habitual thief, the defiler of the preceptor's bed and he who associates with these is the great sinner fifth in all.*
9.3.72: He who kills a brahmin out of fury, greed, fear or hatred or uses heart-rending taunts becomes the slayer of a brahmin.
9.3.73: He who invite? a brahmin and makes him some gift but later on takes it back and criticises him and rebukes him without any fault is the slayer of a brahmin.

9.3.9: If a brahmin learns the Vedas and acquires knowledge of Brahman and Siva, but eschews it later on he commits a sin equal to that of drinking wine.
9.4.0: These are terrible sins like the murder of a brahmin:—abandonment of parents, perjury, lying to brah¬ mins, flesh-eating in regard to the devotees of Siva, eating forbidden food, killing of innocent living beings in the forest, failure to use for charitable purpose the funds left by good men for the sake of brahmins and committing of arson in the forest or village or in the pathway of cows.
9.4.1: The following sins are equal to the theft of gold:—The forfeiture of the entire property of a poor man; the selling of these by a brahmin knowingly done except in a grave emergency—man, woman, elephant, horse, cow, land, silver, cloth, medicinal herbs, juices (or quicksilver) sandal paste, Aguru, camphor, musk, silk garments etc. and misap¬ propriation of deposits kept in trust. The following are sins on a par with that of defiling teacher's bed—the non-disposal of marriageable daughters by giving them in marriage to deserving husbands, having sexual intercourse with the wives of sons and friends or with the sisters, raping virgins; cohabitation with an intoxicated woman or a woman of one's own caste. These are the great sins I have mentioned. Now listen to the minor sins.
9.4.10: Removal of a brahmin's money, transgressor of the rules of inheritance, too much of arrogance, great fury, false prestige, ingratitude.
9.4.11: Debauchery, miserliness, malice towards good men illicit approach to another man's wife, defiling the virgins of good men.
9.4.12: The spoilation of flowers and trees around the tem¬ ple of Siva; even the slightest injury to the people in the hermitage.
9.4.13: The theft of cattle, grain, wealth etc. of the family of servants, theft of base metals, food-grains and milch cattle, dirtying of waters.
9.4.14: Selling of sacrificial parks and ponds, wives and children, pilgrimages and fasts, sacred rites and investiture with sacred thread.
9.4.15: Dependence on dowry, servitude to women, non- protection of the womenfolk, carrying on affairs with women through fraudulent means.
9.4.16: Using bullock constantly as a vehicle through wild jungles, Uccatana (exorcising) and Abhicara (black magic) acceptance of grains as gift, working as a physician.
9.4.17: Engagement in sacred rites to satisfy the palate or the sexual urge, teaching only the text of the Vedas (not the meaning).
9.4.18: For the comparison of the Piincipal and subsidiary sins as mentioned in the previous and present chapters, see Manu Ch. ii. The treatment of the subject in.P is more elaborate.
9.4.19: Eschewing of Brahma and other Vratas and adop¬ tion of ther modes and customs, learning of spurious holy lore, engagement in hair-splitting arguments.
9.4.2: Censuring gods, fire-god, preceptors and virtuous men openly and the kings and his officers indirectly.
9.4.20: Those who have ceased to perform sacrifices to the gods and the manes, those who have abandoned their duties and rites, persons of evil conduct, atheists, sinners, and habitual liars.
9.4.21: He who indulges in sexual intercourse during new moon and full moon days during day time, or in the vagi¬ nal passages of animals, or through other passages or emits semen in water, or cohabits with a woman in her monthly course.
9.4.22: Those who shatter the hopes of obtaining wives, sons and friends; those who speak displeasing words; ruth¬ less persons and those who break agreements.
9.4.23: Those who damage or demolish lakes, wells or water causeways; he who serves different kinds of food among persons sitting in the same row.
9.4.24: The foregoing are some of the minor sins. Men or women guilty of the same are minor sinners, I shall mention some others also. Listen.
9.4.25: Those who cause injury to cows, brahmins, vir¬ gins, master, friends or ascetics are sure to go to hell.
9.4.26: Those who undergo agony due to another man's wife; those who have an eye on another man's wealth; those who steal that and those who make use of false weights.
9.4.27: Those who cause misery to brahmins by means of kicks and blows; the brahmins who serve iSudra women and drink wine due to passion.
9.4.28: Those who are cruel and engaged in sinful acts; those who arc fond of violence and those who perform Dana, Yajfia and other rites as a profession for livelihood.
9.4.29: Those who evacuate their bowels in cowpens, streets, near water and fire, shades of trees, mountains, parks and temples.
9.4.3: Those who are engaged in drinking bouts in hermitages and palaces; those who are in search of weak points in others; those who are in association with others.
9.4.30: Those who block roads by means of bamboos, bricks, logs of wood, horns or poles and those who violate the boundaries of others' fields.
9.4.31: Those who make counterfeit documents, those who are engaged in fraudulent activities, those who indulge in fraud in dealing in food and clothing and in law suits.
9.4.32: The maker, buyer and seller of bows, weapons and darts, he who is merciless to servants and he who ill-treats animals.
9.4.33: He who listens slowly to the words of liars, who is traitor to masters, friends and teachers, a cheat, a fickle- minded and a rogue

9.4.36: Those who voluntarily decide to perform certain rites with self-imposed checks and restraints but leave them off because they have not conquered their sense-organs; those who renounce but again come back to householder's life; breakers of the idols of Siva.

9.5.1: The king who confiscates the properties of brahmins unjustly and passes them on to others certainly falls into hell.
9.5.10: Sin accrues to the fierce robbers ind to those cohabiting with other men's wives. It accrues to the king who indulges in amorous sports with other's women.
9.5.11: If the king does not discriminate between a non¬ thief and a thief and kills the wrong person he is sure to fall in hell.

9.5.14: At the behest of Yama the sinners go to the world o.f Yama in their bodies, which are dragged by Yama's terrible emissaries and are subjected to grief.
9.5.15: For those who regularly observe restraints and disciplined life but who err slightly due to oversight, the preceptor is the chastiser through expiatory rites and not Yama as explained by learned men.
9.5.16: Hence one should perform expiatory rites for the commission of sins. If the sin is not consumed it will not perish even in hundreds of crores of Kalpas.
9.5.17: As a result of the four kinds of sins, all living beings go to Yamaloka. They are helpless.
9.5.18: It shall be known to all living beings whether in the womb, in the process of birth, as children, <outh or middling whether women, man or a eunuch.
9.5.19: Here the result of the auspicious and the inaus¬ picious actions of all embodied beings is being considered by Gitragupta Vasistha and others.
9.5.2: There are no living beings who do not go to Yama's abode. The result of the action must of necessity be undergone. Let that be considered.
9.5.20: Men who have performed auspicious rites who are of gentle minds, endowed with the quality of compassion, go to Yama's abode through the gentle entrance at the East.
9.5.21: Sinners, habitually performing sinful actions and devoid of charitable nature, pass through the terrible path and enter Yama's abode by the southern gate.
9.5.22: It must be known that the multiformed city of Yama'-*®® is situated at a distance of eightysix thousand Yojanas from the Earth.
9.5.23: To men of auspicious deeds it appears to be very near, but to the sinners who go along the terrible path it is situated far off.
9.5.24: Somewhere the cross-roads are full of sharp iron pieces, elsewhere there is a forest-fire; in other places these are hot rocks; in some places snow spreads over it.
9.5.25: Some places are full of fine sand where the persons sink up to the neck; elsewhere it is full of stinking muddy water and some places arc covered with burning balls of dry cowdung.
9.5.26: Different places are infested with different terrible beasts of prey such as lions, wolves, tigers and huge pythons or terrible mosquitoes or huge leeches.
9.5.27: Terrible flies, extremely poisonous serpents, herds of elephants in rut mad and mighty, crushing everything under their feet infest the paths.

9.5.3: They go on, burnt and scorched by lightning falls and pierced through by heavy showers of arrows.
9.5.30: They are scorched and burnt by the showers of burning coal, the falling terrible thunderbolts and meteors.

9.5.33: They shrink and wither when oppressed by the rough and chill wind all round.

9.5.36: They have by this time become ghosts. They have no cloth on. Their throats, lips and palates are parched. They are frightened of terror. They are hungry and feel a burning sensation all over.
9.5.37: Some are bound with fetters and forced to keep their legs lifted up. They are dragged again and again by the extraordinarily powerful emissaries of Yama.
9.5.38: Others with downcast faces are against the chest. They are distressed. They are dragged with a rope fastened to their tresses.
9.5.39: Men in supine position are dragged along the thorny path or that covered with burning coal, by means of a goad clutching at their foreheads.
9.5.4: The hands of some are tied behind and they are hit in the belly. Others are completely bound with iron fetters. Still others are nailed in their hands.

9.5.5: The noses of others arc bored and ropes arc tied through them and they are dragged. Similarly others have their cheeks and lips bored and are dragged by ropes.

They vainly beg for happiness. But those who had made charitable gilts in the world have all the food and drink necessary for this journey and go ahead to Yama's abode happily.

9.6.24: After having proclaimed their evil actions, Yama, Dharmaraja speaks to the messengers thus, for wiping off the sins of those kings.

9.6.33: In the hellish hres, the sinners are roasted and dried up by diverse tortures till their action is exhausted completely.
9.6.34: Just as metals are melted in fire to remove their impurities so also sinners are put in hells in order to remove their sins.
9.6.35: The hands are tightly tied and the men are battered. Then they are suspended from the branches of tall trees by the attendants ofYama.
9.6.36: Then they are pushed by the servants till they begin to oscillate a Yojana unconscious by their rapidity.
9.6.37: Even as they are suspended in mid air, iron hundred Bharas in weight is tied to their feet by the emissaries of Yama.
9.6.38: Afflicted by such a heavy weight the sinners begin to think about their evil actions and keep quiet and motion¬ less.
9.6.39: Then the sinners are beaten with goads of fiery colour and terrible iron rods by the terrible servants of Yama.
9.6.4: Then they are again smeared with glowing acid more unbearable than fire.
9.6.40: Their limbs are cut and smothered, gradually torn and severed and smeared with molten metal. They are then roasted like brinjal in red-hot iron cauldrons. They are then cast into wells full of filth, swarms of worms or in tanks full of putrid fat and blood. They are eaten by worm and crows with beaks strong as iron.
9.6.41: Dogs, mosquitoes, wolves and tigers of terrible and hideous faces too devour them. They are roasted like fish over glowing heaps of coal.
9.6.42: Due to their sinful actions men are pierced through with sharp spears. They are put in oil extracting machines called Cakra and crushed like gingelly seeds and beaten into pulp. They are fried in iron cauldrons red hot in the blazing sunlight.
9.6.43: They are fried in boiling oil in cauldrons again and again. Their tongues, chests and feet are struck in many ways.
9.6.44: Here the tortures to the body are very severe. Men thus go from one hell to another and are tortured in all the hells.
9.6.45: O vyasa, terrible tortures are inflicted in diverse ways in all the hells by Yama's emissaries. They are grievous and painful to every part of the body.
9.6.46: Their mouths are filled with the burning coals and again with acid red hot, copper hot clarified butter and oil and they are beaten afterwards.
9.6.47: They are filled with faeces and worms and arc forced to embrace the red hot fierce iron-silk cotton tree.
9.6.48: They are then beaten on the back with heated hammer. Their heads and their limbs are crushed with too blunt tooth-edged strong scissors. They are thus tortured by their own actions. Their flesh is eaten and their blood is drunk by them.
9.6.49: Those who fed and nurtured only themselves and never made any gift of food or drink are crushed with iron rods like sugarcane.
9.6.5: In the terrible hell Asitalavana they arc cut into pieces. Their limbs are pierced through with needles. They are staked on to heated spearheads.
9.6.50: Tossed about many times their bodies do not perish but are severely pained. They become u.sed to bear the pleasure or pain.
9.6.51: In the hell Nirucchvasa they are forced to stand without breathing, for a long time. In the hell Ucchvasa they are hit and thrashed in a house of sand.
9.6.52: In the hell Raurava they arc made to cry and inflicted pain by various tortures. Due to the tortures in the hell, Maharaurava, even great men cry.

9.6.55: O sage, in the hell kumbhipaka sinners of ruthless misdeeds are fried in unbearable boiling oil.
9.6.56: The sinners are felled and dragged along various torturing places again and again in the hell named Lalabhaka.
9.6.57: Sinners devoid of merit are beaten by Yama*s servants. They are hurled into the torturous hell Sucimukha.
9.6.58: They are put into iron pots. They breathe hard and slow. They are scorched by great fire, as if by their own sins.
9.6.6: They are tied tightly with ropes and arc rolled on rocks and harassed. They are cast into deep gloomy wells. They are subjected to bee-bites.
9.6.7: When their bodies are cut, bitten and gnawed by worms in a hundred places, they are hurled into wells of pun¬ gent acid.
9.6.8: In the blazing hell the distressed sinners, shriek and run about here and there scorched by its flames.
9.6.9: People are clubbed and tied together with mouths resting on shoulders and hands brought through the hollow and tied with nooses and ropes to the back. Such bundles of bodies are seen in the Mahajvala undergoing tortures.
9.7.0: Dragged and rolled through rough and coarse rocks, beaten and burnt like straw, the sinners of ruthless conduct, are tortured.

9.7.11: Red hot iron clubs are thrust into their mouths. They are helplessly forced to gnaw at it. They arc then beaten with iron threshing rods.

9.7.13: He who follows false scriptures goes to the hell Dvijihva. He is tortured by the tongue-like ploughshares extending to one and a half kilometres.

9.7.16: Sinners who indulge in illicit union with other's wives are forced to embrace red-hot iron images of those women with whom they had illicit relation and struck in various ways.
9.7.17: Images of those men are made of red hot iron and the erring women are forced to embrace those images. They cry and shriek.

9.7.21: The organs wherewith men defile or harass women are respectively tortured.

9.7.40: Men who perform auspicious rites here, whose minds are gentle and who are merciful pass through the terrible path of Yama happily.
9.7.41: He who makes gifts of sandals of leather or wood to leading brahmins goes happily to the abode of Yama on a great horse.

9.7.45: The founders of hermitages of ascetics and Rest houses for the orphans feel as if they play in the house.
9.7.46: Worshippers of the gods, fire-god brahmins and their parents go along that path as they please. They are honoured on the way.
9.7.47: Those who gift lamps, go brightly illuminating all the ten quarters. By giving dwellings and asylums they go without ailments on the way.
9.7.48: Those who habitually serve their preceptors go without difficulty. They get ample rest on the way. Those who gift musical instruments to brahmins go happily feeling at home on the way.
9.7.49: Givers of cows go along the path flourishing with all their desires. They get those food-stuflfs and drinks which they give away here, on that path also.
9.7.5: By giving water for washing the feet one goes along the path full of water. He who gifts oils for massaging the feet goes on horseback along that way.
9.7.50: O Vyasa, Yama never comes near the man who always makes gifts of water for washing the feet, oil for massa¬ ging, lamps, foodstufls and dwellings.
9.7.51: By making gifts of gold and gems he crosses all impassable hurdles. By gifting silver and oxen he goes to Yamaloka happily.
9.7.52: By these and similar charitable gifts people go happily to Yama's abode. They attain different pleasures in the heaven.
9.7.53: Food gives blood, flesh, fat and semen and out of semen living beings are born. Hence the universe is identical with food.
9.7.54: Hungry men are not delighted even if they possess these things viz—gold, gems, horses, elephants, women, garlands, sandal paste and the like.
9.7.55: All persons, the child in the womb, the new born babe, the child, the middle aged man, the old man, the gods, the danavas or Raksasas desire food.
9.7.56: All embodied beings die when scorched by the fire of hunger. That is why it is glorified that there is great merit in the charitable gift of food.
9.7.57: If a man performs holy and sacred rites after being nourished with the food gifted by someone, the merit of the sacred rites is shared half and half by the two—namely by the giver of food and the performer of the rites. There is no doubt in this.
9.7.58: The giver of charitable gift of food obtains here and hereafter whatever means of pleasure there are in the three worlds such as gems, women and vehicles.
9.7.59: Even by putting one's family to inconvenience and trouble one should give food to a mendicant brahmin of noble soul, if one wishes for one's prosperity.
9.7.6: He who gives food to a suppliant brahmin in distress actually makes an excellent deposit facilititing his benefit in the other world.
9.7.7: A householder, desirous of prosperity shall worship a brahmin who has approached him at the proper time for his livelihood, or who is travel-weary and comes to his house as a guest.
9.7.8: O Vyasa, a giver of food, of good conduct and free from malice, is honoured. A gift of food never goes in- vain be it to a dog or a person who cooks dogs. If a person eschews anger that surges up he derives happiness here and hereafter. He should not encourage it even if it is natural. One shall try to eschew it somehow.

9.8.18: Even after committing a great sin if a man gives food to the needy he becomes rid of all sins. He goes to heaven.

9.8.21: O great sage, if a person listens to this or nar¬ rates this at the performance of Sraddha to brahmins, it results in a never-ending gift of food to the Pitri.
9.8.22: Hence one should make gifts of drinking water¬ sheds lovingly and unrestrictedly. Making of water bases, tanks etc. is the cause of great bliss.
9.8.23: A well that abounds in water removes half of the sin of the man who causes it to be dug.
9.8.24: If cows drink and good men and brahmins make use of the water in a water-base dug by a man, the whole family is redeemed.
9.8.25: He who dig a lake attains an endless merit. The wise say that it is the fruit of virtue, wealth and love.

9.8.3: Trees honour and worship the gods through flowers, the Pitfs through fruits, and the guests through shade.
9.8.30: The Kinnaras, the serpents, the Raksasas, the gods, the Gandharvas, the human beings and the sages depend upon trees.
9.8.31: While in bloom or when they bear fruits, the trees delight human beings. They are as sons by way of virtue in this world and hereafter.
9.8.32: These people never fail to attain heaven—viz. the digger of lakes, the planter of trees, the brahmin who performs sacrifices and those who speak truth.

9.8.38: The sages have attained heaven travelling in aerial chariots along with the celestial damsels. Truth shall be ever spoken, for there is nothing greater than Truth.
9.8.39: In the deep, extensive and pure eddy, the holy centre of Truth, one shall mentally take one*s ceremonial ablution. That i$ said to be the highest bliss.

9.21.24: He begot of her ten thousand sons Haryasvas. At the instance of Narada they became detached from the world.
9.21.25: On hearing of it Daksa again begot of her a thousand sons SubalaSvas.
9.21.26: Thanks to the instructions of the same sage they too followed the footsteps of their brothers. Unattached and following the path of mendicants they never returned to their parents.
9.21.27: On hearing of it he became very furious and cursed the sage thus— O wretch, fond of quarrels, you will never stay permanently anywhere. *
9.21.29: Consoled by Brahma, O great sage he afterwards created women endowed with qualities and in the form of great flames.®
9.21.3: Asuras and others were born of the daughters of Daksa and had become famous. The universe was filled with them.
9.21.30: O great brahmin, the subjects thereafter were born of sexual union. The creation prior to this was through mental concepts, visualisation and touch.
9.21.31: O Suta, it behoves you to clear this doubt of mine. This is also surprising how he attained the status of of the father-in-law of Soma.
9.21.32: Birth and destruction happen everyday among the mortals. O sage, in every Kalpa these, Daksa and others are born again.
9.21.33: He who knows this mode of creation of Daka of the mobile and immobile beings becomes endowed with pro¬ geny and longevity. After death he is honoured in the heavenly region.
9.21.34: The Verses 47, 48 are repeatecL See Gh. 31. Verses 17, 18.
9.21.35: O son of Suta, tell me quickly about the details of the creation of the gods, Danavas, Gandharvas, serpents and Rakasas.
9.21.36: When the creation did not multiply, the patriarch asked the daughter of Virana, endowed with penance, for the purpose of creation
9.21.37: He created different people by the process of copulation. O intelligent one, listen to them. I shall ex¬ plain in brief.
9.21.38: Uniting with her, the powerful patriarch begot of Virini five thousand sons.
9.21.4: Narada, son of Brahma, had heard at the Satra that the creation can take place only through KaSyapa in the daughters of Daka. So, on seeing the created sons, the sage Narada addressed them thus.

9.21.6: Thus addressed by him they all proceeded to know the direction by means of their power. Without being able to reach their end they never returned to their father*s house.
9.21.7: On knowing that he created five himdred sons, Narada, the visualiser of all, spoke to them also.
9.21.8: How can you create without knowing the extent of the world? All of you are childish. What creation do you propose to make?

9.22.0: Ever since, O sage, if a brother goes in quest of a brother he perishes. That should not be done by any learned man.
9.22.1: Realising that his sons had perished, the patriarch Daksa cursed the noble soul Narada in anger.
9.22.10: "O wretch, fond of quarrels, you will never stay anywhere permanently. Qiiarrel will always occur among the people where you happen to be present."
9.22.11: We have heard that Daksa the patriarch was consoled by Brahma afterwards and that he begot of Virini sixty daughters.'
9.22.12: He gave ten of them to Dharma; thirteen to Kayapa; twentyseven to the moon and four to Aristanemi.
9.22.13: Two to the son of Brahma, two to Ahgiras and two to the learned Kr<ai5va. Now listen to their names.
9.22.14: O sage, the wives of Dharma are Arundhati, Vasu, Yami, Lamba, Bhanu, Marutvati, Sahkalpa, Muhurta, Sadhya and Visva. Now listen to their children. Vive- devas are the sons of Visva, and Sadhya gave birth to Sadh/as.
9.22.15: Marutvats were born of Marutvati, Vasus were born of Vasu; the suns were born of Bhanu and the Muhurtajas were born of Muhurta.
9.22.16: According to the present text Daksa had sixty daughters. Of these he gave 10 to Dharma, to Kasyapa, 27 to Soma, 4 to Ari;tane- min 2 to Brahmaputra, 2 to Ahgiras and 2 Krsasva. But the assignment is not uniform in all the Puranas. For instance MP (5. 13-14) assigns
9.22.17: Aya, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Anala, Pratyusa and Prabhasa are the eight Vasus by name.
9.22.18: Aya's sons arc Vaitanda, Srama, Santa and Muni. Dhruva's son was lord Kala influencing the worlds.
9.22.19: Manohara's sons were Sasira, Prana and
9.22.2: His sons were Sakha, Visakha and Naigameya. The son of Krttikas was called Karttikeya,®
9.22.21: Brhaspati's sister was a woman of excellence, well-versed in Yoga and she traversed the entire world maintaining celibacy. She became the wife ot Prabhasa the eighth of Vasus. O fortunate one, Viwakarman the patriarch was born of him.'
9.22.22: He built the aerial chariots of all god s. He is a great Atman whose craft is emulated and made use of by men too.
9.22.23: According to another version his wife Sarupa gave birth to crores of Rudras such as Raivata, Aja, Bhava, Bhima, Varna, Ugra, Vrsakapi, Ajaikapad, Ahirbudhnya, Bahurupa, Mahat etc. Eleven of them are important. O sage, listen to their names.
9.22.24: The patriarch Viivakarma, son of Vasu Prabhasa, was the craftsman of the gods ancl entrusted with the work of building chariots, ornaments, palac<'s etc. MP 5. 27-V8, Sec P. 389 note 295.
9.22.25: These eleven are the Rudras, lords of the three worlds viz: — Ajaikapad, Ahirbudhnya, Tvastr, the powerful Rudrahara of many forms, Tryambaka, Aparajita, Vr§akapi, ambhu, Kapardin and Raivata.®
9.22.26: Thus a hundred Rudras of immense prowess have been mentioned to you. Now listen to the names of Kayapa's wives, O excellent sage.
9.22.27: O brahmin, they are Aditi, Surasa, Aristela, Danti, Surabhi, Vinata, Ila, Tamra, Krodhavasa, Kadru and Muni. Now listen to the names of their sons. In the previous excellent Manvantara twelve excellent gods were born.
9.22.28: They are Tusitas. During the intervening period of the Vaivasvata and Gaksusa Manvantaras they consulted one another for the welfare of the worlds. After meeting together they spoke — "We will enter Aditi and be born. This will happen for the welfare of the gods." After con¬ ferring they were born of Aditi daughter of Daksa and Kasyapa son of Marici. Visnu and Indra were born again.
9.22.29: They along with Aryaman, Dhatr, Tvastr, Pusan, Vivasvat, Savitr, Mitravaruna, Arhsa, Bhaga and Atilejas are the twelve Adityas. Those who were born before as Tusitas were born again as the twelve Adityas in the Gaksusa Manvantara, O aunaka thus the names of Aditi's sons have been mentioned to you. •
9.22.3: Diptis of immeasurable splendour became the children of the twentyseven women of sacred rites and the wives of Soma.
9.22.30: The children of Aristanemi's wives were shcteen in number. "O celestial sage, the learned Krsava had many sons. Four of them are known as Devapraharana. O sage, in his wife Arcis, Dhumrakesa too was born.
9.22.31: Two wives were Svadha and Sati of whom Svadha was the elder and Sati the younger. Svadha gave birth to the Pitrs and Sati to the Atharvarigirasaveda.
9.22.32: At the end of a thousand Yugas these will be born again. All the groups of the gods are ihirtythree.
9.22.33: Just as the sun rises and sets every day so also the groups of gods are born in every Yuga.
9.22.34: We have heard that Hiranyakasipu and Hiranyaksa were born as the sons of Dili and Kasyapa.
9.22.35: Siihhika their daughter became the wife of Vipra- citti. The four sons of Hiranyakasipu were famous for their strength and prowess.
9.22.36: They are Anuhrada, Hrada, Sariihrada and Prahlada. The youngest Prahlada wai a devotee of Visnu.
9.22.37: Puloman and Mahisa were the sons of Anuhrada born of Surya. Hrada's wife Dhamani gave birth to Vatapi and Ilvala.
9.22.38: Samhrada's wife Ryti gave birth to Paftcajana. Virocana was the son of Prahlada. Bali was born of his queen Devi.
9.22.39: O great sage, Bali begot hundred sons of his wife Asana. He was a great devotee of Siva. He engaged himself in the activities of devotion to Siva. He was chari¬ tably inclined and liberal-minded. He attained meritorious fame and austerity. His son Bana was foremost among the devotees of Siva. By propititing Siva he attained the leader¬ ship of Ganas.
9.22.4: The story of Bana has already been heard by you. In the battle Krna was delighted with him.
9.22.40: Prabha was the daughter of Svarbhanu. Sad was the daughter of Puloman. So also Upadanavi, Hayasira and Sarmistha were daughters of Vrsaparvan. Puloma and Pulomika were the daughters of Vaisvanara. They were the wives of Kasyapa son of Marici and had many heroic sons.
9.22.41: Kalakhanjas, the powerful sons of Puloma, lived in Hiranyapura.® They could not be killed either by the Danavas or by the gods.
9.22.42: Vipracitti's sons, born of Sirhhika, were later killed by Arjuna by the grace of Brahma.
9.22.43: Due to the intermixture of Daityas and Danavas the.se sons became valorous and famous as Saimhikeyas. They arc thirteen in number.
9.22.44: They were the very powerful Rahu and Salya, Bala, Mahabala, Vatapi, Namuci, Ilvala, Svasrpa, Ajika, Naraka, Kalanabha, Saramana and Sarakalpa. These in¬ creased their races.
9.22.45: Many sons and grandsons were born of them increas¬ ing the race of Danu. Being innumerable they are not mentioned in detail.
9.22.46: In the family of Sarhhrada the Daiteyas Nivatakavacas and Maruts were born and they were purified by penance.
9.22.47: Sanmukha and others are glorified as the sons of Tamra. Kaki, iSyeni, Bhasi, Sugrivi, Suki, Grdhrika, Asvi, and
9.22.48: This city of the Pauloina.s and Kalakhanjas (or Kalakeyas) as mentioned in the Mhabliarata (Vana P. GLXXIII. 13) and the Kathasaritsagara (XLV. 135) stood on the sca-routc leading to PalSla. Its exact locus remains still unidentified.
9.22.49: Syienl gave birth to vultures, Bhasi to Bhasas Grdhri to Grdhrakas. SukI gave birth to parrots and Sugrlvl to auspicious birds.
9.22.5: Tamra the beloved of Kasyapa gave birth to horses, camels and donkeys. Thus the family of Tamra has been described to you.
9.22.5.22.20: Vinata had two sons Aruna and Garuda. The latter was the most excellent among birds. He was terrible by virtue of his activities.
9.22.50: Surasa gave birth to a thousand serpents of immeasurable power. They had many hoods. They were powerful enough to traverse the sky, the important among them were the kings Sesa, Vasuki and Taksaka, Airavata, Mahapadma, Kambala and Asvatara. The sons of Aila were Padma, Karkotaka, Dhanafijaya, Mahanila, Mahakarna, Dhrtarastra, Balahaka, Kuhara, Puspadanta, Durmukha, Sumukha, Khararoman, Kharapani and many others.
9.22.51: Krodhavasa gave birth to many who. were the fanged animals and birds both of land and water. Vara's sons were animals.
9.22.6: Anayusa's sons were fifty. They were very strong. The chief amongst them were Bala, Vrtta, Viksara and Brhan.
9.22.7: Surabhi gave birth to rabbits and buffaloes; Ila to trees, creepers, spreading vines and all kinds of grass; Khasa gave birth to Yaksa and Raksasas, Muni gave birth to the celestial damsels. Arista gave birth to serpents more ex¬ cellent than human beings in their power.
9.22.8: O great sages, thus the descendants of Kasyapa have been explained to you. They had hundreds of sons and grandsons.
9.22.9: Such is the creation as mentioned in the Man- vantara, Svarocisa, O dear. Now I shall describe the creation as evolved by Brahman while oflering oblations in the ela¬ borate Varuna sacrifice in the great Vaivasvata Manvantara. All the Brahmarsis born in the beginning, Pitamaha made his mental sons. When a great fight ensued between the gods and the Danavas, Diti lost all her sons. She approached Kasyapa and propitiated him. The delighted Kasyapa asked her to choose a boon as she pleased. She chose the boon that she be favoured with a son of immeasurable power capable of slaying Indra.
9.23.0: The pious fair-comlexioned lady conceived. She began to observe celibacy and other restraints.
9.23.1: \fter impregnating Diti, Kasyapa of noble sacred rites went away satisfied for the performance of penance.
9.23.10: Indra waited for finding out a weak point in her. He found one such when the period of hundred years was short by a year.
9.23.11: Due to the gravity of the event destined to happen, once Diti did not wash her feet. She went to sleep with head hanging down.
9.23.12: In the meantime Indra entered her belly with the thunderbolt. He cut off the foetus into seven pieces.
9.23.13: While being split into seven the foetus began to cry in seven different tones. Indra told the foetus "Do not cry, Do not cry" repeatedly. He cut them again but they did not die.
9.23.14: O sage, being felled down they told him with

9.23.16: O brahmin sage, at the will of Siva, they eschewed their Daitya nature. They were accepted by Indra with due fraternity.
9.23.17: In the name of Maruts they became gods of great prowess. Thus traversing the sky the fortynine Maruts be¬ came assistants of Indra.
9.23.18: When they flourished, Visnu the patriarch, offered them kingdoms beginning with Prthu. Listen to that.
9.23.19: O great sage, I have explained the creation of living beings to you. Listen to the division of kingdoms. I shall explain that duly now.
9.23.2: After crowning Prthu the son of Vena in the emperorship, Brahma began to assign the kingdoms in due order.
9.23.20: He crowned Soma in the kingdom of birds,
9.23.21: He crowned Varuna in the kingdom of waters; Vairavana as the lord of kings; Visnu as the lord of Aditvas and Pavaka as the lord of Vasus.
9.23.22: He crowned Daksa as the lord of patriarchs, Indra as the lord of Maruts, and Prahlada of great strength as the lord of Daityas and Danavas.
9.23.23: He crowned Vaivasvata Yama in the kingdom of Pitrs, Matrs, Vratas, Mantras and cows.
9.23.24: He crowned the trident-bearing Siva, in the king¬ dom of Yaksas, Raksasas, kings, goblins and ghosts.
9.23.25: He crowned Himavat as the lord of mountains, the ocean of rivers, the tiger of deer and Bull as the 'lord of cows.
9.23.26: He crowned the banyan tree in the kingdom of plants and trees. Thus the kingdom was assigned every¬ where by the lord of subjects.
9.23.27: The lord of the universe, the soul of all, established the son of patriarch Vairaja in the kingdom in the east.
9.23.28: Similarly, O great king, he established Sudhanvan, son of Kardama, the patriarch, in the kingdom in the south.
9.23.29: The lord directed and assigned the unfailing noble- minded son of Rajas, Ketumat as the king in the kingdom in the west.
9.23.3: He crowned the indefatigable son of Parjanya the patriarch, Hiranyaroman, in the kingdom in the north.
9.23.30: O great sage, six Manus have already been mentioned to you viz. Svayambhuva, Svarocisa, Uttama, Tamasa, Raivata and Gakua. The present Manu is called Vaivasvata, O great sage.
9.23.31: The Manus of future are Savarni, Raucya, Brahmasavarni, Dharmasavarni, Rudrasavarni, Devasavarni and Indraasvarni. All these constitute the Manus of the past, present and future. These have been enumerated by me as I have heard.
9.23.32: O sage, these fourteen Manvantaras extending over the period past, present and the future have been mentioned to you. A Kalpa consisting of a thousand Yugas is constituted by these.
9.23.33: O Saunaka, listen. I shall explain the sages, their sons and the gods; all are famous. Listen with pleasure.
9.23.34: Marici, Atri, the holy lord Ahgiras, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya and Vasistha — these seven are Brahma's sons.
9.23.35: O sage, the seven sages are in the northern quarter. In the Svayambhuva Manvantara there were the gods named Yamas.
9.23.36: The ten noble-souled sons of Svayambhuva Manu were — Agnidhra, Agnibahu, Medha, Medhatithi, Vasu, Jyoti§mat, Dhrtimat, Havya, Savana and Subhra. O great sage, the Indra there was Yajfia.
9.23.37: Thus O dear, the first divine Manvantara has been mentioned to you. I shall explain the second one. Know as it is.
9.23.38: In the second Svarocisa Manvantara these must be known as the great sages, viz-Orjastambha, Parastambha, Rsabha, Vasumat, Jyotismat, Dyutimat and the seventh Rocismat. Then the Indra was Rocana. The gods were known as Tusitas.
9.23.39: O great sage, the ten noble-minded sons of Svarocisa Manu, all of great heroism and exploits were Harighna, Sukrti, Jyotis, Ayomurti, Ayasmaya, Prathita, Manasyu, Nabha and Surya.
9.23.4: O sage, the second Manvantara has been men¬ tioned by me. I shall explain the third one. Know it factually.
9.23.40: Vasisjha's seven sons famous as Vasisthas and Hiranyagarbha's sons of great splendour known as Orjas are mentioned as the sages. Uttama the Manu had ten sons, O great sage.
9.23.41: They were Isa, Crjita, Crja, Madhu, Madhava Suci, Sukravaha, Nabhasa, Nabha and Rsabha. The gods were Satyavedaruta and others. O sage, the Indra then was Satyajit. He was the ruler of the three worlds.
9.23.42: The great third Manvantara has been explained. O sage, listen. I shall mention the fourth Manvantara.
9.23.43: The seven sages were Gargya, Prthu, Vagmin, Janya, Dhata, Kapinaka and the seventh Kapivat. The groups of gods were Satyas.
9.23.44: The Indra there was TriSikha. O sage, listen to the names of Manu's sons. The ten sons of great rites of the Mam' Tamasa were Dyutipota, Sautapasya, Tapahula, Tapana, Taporali, Akalmasa, Dhanvin, Khadgin, Mahat and Rsi.
9.23.45: The fourth Manvantara of Tamasa Manu has been mentioned to you. O dear, now listen to the great fifth Manvantara.
9.23.46: Devabahu, Jaya, the sage VedaSiras, Hiran- yaroman, Parjanya, Drdhva Bahu, Somapa — Thcse and others constituted the seven sages. They were engaged in truth. The gods were Bhutarajasas of the nature of performing penance.
9.23.47: Osage, Arjuna, Pahktivindhya and others shall be known as his sons. They are endowed with great penance. They stay on the mountain Meru.
9.23.48: The future Manus in this Kalpa will be seven. The future great sages will also be seven in each Manvantara in the heaven.
9.23.49: Rama, Vyasa, Atrcya, Diptimat, SubahuSruta, Bharadvaja, and the lustrous Asvatthaman son of Drona will be seven sages in this Manvantara.
9.23.5: !§aradvat son of Gautama, Gautama, Krpa, Kauika, Galava, Ruru and Kayapa will be future seven sages. The future gods are three in number as mentioned by Svayambhu. They are the sons of the noble-souled KaSyapa the son of Marici. Bali the son of Virocana will become their Indra.
9.23.50: O iSaunaka, the future ten sons of Savarni the Manu will be Visahga, Avanivat, Sumanta, Dhrtimat, Vasu, Suri, Sura, Visnu, Raja and Sumati. Thus the eighth Manvantara has been mentioned. Now listen to the ninth Manvantara.
9.23.51: I shall mention Dakasavarni Manu at the out¬ set. Listen. Medhatithi, Paulastya, Vasu, Kasyapa, Jyoti§mat, Bhargava, Dhrtimat, Ahgiras, Savana son of Vasijha, Havya son of Atri, and Pulaha — these seven are the sages in the Rauhita Manvantara. O great sage, the groups of gods are three.

Havi$mat, Pulaha, Prakfti, Bhargava, Aya, Mukti, Atreya and the imperishable Vasi$tha along with the seven great sages viz, ' Paulastya, Prayati, Bhamara, Kasyapa, Angira, Anenasa, and Satya. Those known as Dvi§imant are the groups of gods.

9.23.55: In the eleventh Manvantara of the third Savarni there arc seven sages. Understand them as they are glorified by me.
9.23.56: Havismat Kasyapa, Vapusmat Varuna, Atreya, Vasistha, Anaya, Angiras, Carudhrsya, Paulastya, Nihsvara, Taijasa Agni. The first seven are the sages and the last three groups are of gods.

9.23.60: In the fourteenth Manvantara of Satya Manu the seven sages are Agnidhra Kayapa, Magadha, Paulastya Atibahya Bhargava, 3uci Angirasa, Yukta Atreya, *Ajita grandson of Vasitha* and Pulaha. They are the final seven sages. The gods are the holy Caksusas. 3uci will become In<;Jra.
9.23.61: Afier getting up early in the morning the repeti¬ tion of the names of these sages of the past and future increases the happiness of men.
9.23.62: O great sage, listen. The groups of gods are five. The sons of this Manu are — Tarangabhiru, Budhna, Tanugra, Anugra, Abhimanin Pravina, Viu, Sankrandana, Tejasvin, and Sabala.
9.23.63: These were mentioned to Vyasa by Sanatkumara of great splendour. When the thousand Yugas are complete they, of good penance, return to Brahmaloka when their task of protecting the people is over. Each Manvantara consists of seventy one Yugas with some period left over.
9.23.64: These fourteen Manus are glorified. In each Man¬ vantara there is re-creation after annihilation.
9.23.65: There all the living beings are burnt by the sun's rays. O sage, all of them enter Visnu at the end of Kalpas along with the Adityas. Vinu then creates all living beings. This happens again and again.
9.23.7: Lord Rudra annihilates them I shall explain it at the end of Vaivasvata Kalpa. Thus I have mentioned all about the Manvantaras to you. It is a,holy narrative condu- sive to wealth and increase of the family.
9.23.8: Due to the unbearable heat of her husband she in her prime of youth was dissatisfied.
9.23.9: Being scorched and not being able to hear the brilliance of the lustrous sun, the fair-complexioned lady was excited and sorrowful.
9.24.0: On seeing the brilliance of the sun as unbearable as the fire at the final dissolution she created Ghaya of herself.
9.24.1: She of illusory form told Sarhjfia: "O sweet-smiled auspicious lady, what shall I do for you, please tell me".
9.24.10: "Welfare unto you. I go to my father's house alone. Indeed you have to stay in this house without aberration.
9.24.11: These two well-behaved sons and this pretty girl should be happily protected if you wish to please me."
9.24.12: "O lady, I shall brook their misdeeds even as much as pulling out my hair. I shall make no complaint to you. O goddess, you can go away happily."
9.24.13: Ashamed on being addressed thus, the lady went to her father's house but was rebuked by him. He urged her again and again to return to her husband.
9.24.14: She assumed the form of a mare. Going to Northern Kurus she wandered among the people.
9.24.15: Though requested by Sarfijfta, Ghaya did not love the elder children. She loved her own son more and fondled him always.
9.24.16: The younger brother Yama could not hear that. He did not forgive. Ever since childhood he was furious and and ill-tempered due to the gravity of what was destined to happen later.
9.24.17: Due to excessive anger she cursed — "Let your leg fall off". Yama approached his father with palms joined in reverence and said.
9.24.18: "I was agitated due to Chaya's words. I am sorry and frightened of the curse. I had only said that a mother shall have impartial and equal love for all her children. She has lost affection for us. She nurtures only the youngest one. Hence I raised my foot. It behoves you to forgive me. O lord of gods, O foremost among the refulgent ones, I have been cursed by my mother. O lord of rays, let not my leg fall off by your grace."
9.24.19: O son, there shall be a great cause for this. That was why you too who know virtue and speak the truth had been infuriated.
9.24.2: Her words will come up true and you will also be saved. Have no doubt, O deer, cheer up your mind, O lord.
9.24.20: O great sage, after saying thus to his son Yama, the sun angrily spoke to Chaya.
9.24.21: O beloved wife, O evil-minded angry lady, what it is that you have done? Why do you love one son more? You shall tell me.
9.24.22: On hearing the words of the sun she told him the truth. Scorched by him she consoled him thus.
9.24.23: I shall change your form. I shall make it pleasingly brilliant.
9.24.24: The sage Tvastr put him on the turner's lathe and sharpened him further. His blazing form was slightly redu¬ ced in brilliance.
9.24.25: He assumed the form of a horse and approached her for sexual indulgence with her who could not be overwhel¬ med by any living being due to her lustre and observance of restraint.
9.24.26: O sage, in the course of the sexual activity she suspected him to be another man. Hence she received the semen through the mouth into the nostril.
9.24.27: Thence were born the twin gods ASvins, the fore¬ most among physicians. They are known as Nasatyas and Dasras.
9.24.28: The sun showed his pleasingly splendid form to them. On seeing her husband she was extremely delighted.
9.24.29: The chaste lady returned to the house with her husband with the face beaming with pleasure. The pair rejoiced more than before.
9.24.3: This incident distressed the mind of Yama. As pious king he gladdened the subjects virtuously.
9.24.30: Yama of great lustre attained the lordship of the names and the guardianship of the quarters.
9.24.31: Savarni Manu became the patriarch. In the Savarnika Manvantara he will become the future Manu by virtue of his action.
9.24.32: The lord is performing penance even today on the top of Meru*i. Their younger sister, the famous Yami, became the most excellent river Yamuna, the sanctifier of all the worlds. 9.36.35: Urged by Indra, the wind-god approached splen¬ dour and addressed it, "Who are you?" The splendour too put the same question to him.
9.36.36: Thus asked by the big mass of splendour the
9.36.37: Everything in the universe, mobile or immobile, is woven like warp and woof into me. I am the support of everything. I move the entire universe.'*
9.36.38: Then the great splendour said; — ''If you are com¬ petent to move, O wind-god, please move this blade of grass I have set before you. Move it as you please."
9.36.39: Then wind-god put forth all his efforts. But the blade of grass did not stir from its position. Then he was put to shame.
9.36.4: The wind-god went silently to the assembly of Indi a. There he narrated the details of his discomfiture.
9.36.40: "False is our pride that we are the lords. In fact we are helpless, insignificant creatures."
9.36.41: Then Indra sent all the gods. When they could not realise anything Indra himself went there.
9.36.42: On seeing Indra come, the unbearable splendour vanished immediately. Indra was surprised.
9.36.43: Then Indra thought to himself again and again — "I seek refuge in him alone whose conduct is such as this."
9.36.44: In the meantime, in order to bless them am'* remove their arrogance, Siva, the embodied form of unde ceitful mercy, existence, knowledge and bliss, manifested her¬ self on the ninth day of the bright half of the month Caitra when the sun was in the middle of the day.
9.36.45: Shining among the mass of.splendour she bright¬ ened the quarters with her brilliance. She enlightened the god.s, saying "I alone am Brahman."
9.36.46: In her four hands she held boons, noose, goad and the mystic gesture of protection. She was served by the Vedas and looked beautiful and proud of her blooming youth.
9.36.47: She wore red garments and red garlands. Red sandal paste was smeared over her body. She was as dazzling as a crore of cupids. Her lustre was that of a crorc moons.
9.36.48: The great Maya, in the form of the immanent soul of all, the cosmic witness of all living beings, and the great Brahman, spoke.
9.36.49: Neither Brahma nor Visnu nor $iva the slayer of
9.36.5: The great Brahman, the great light in the form of the two Pranavas, I alone am. I am all. There is none other beside me.
9.36.50: Though devoid of form 1 possess forms. I consti¬ tute all principles. I am eternal and my attributes cannot be disputed. I am both the cause and the effect.
9.36.51: Sometimes I have the form of a woman, sometimes of a man. Sometimes both. I am goddess assuming all forms.
9.36.52: I am the creator, the protector and the destroyer of the world. I am the enchantress of the universe.
9.36.53: All the Saktis — Kali, Lak$mi and Sarasvati as well as others are born of my parts. So also the arts originate from me.
9.36.54: Just as a magician makes the wooden doll of a woman dance so also I the goddess make all living beings dance.
9.36.55: Being afraid of me the wind blows, the fire-god burns and the guardians of the quarters carry on their duties.
9.36.56: Independent that I am, I sportively bestow victory on the gods sometimes and on the Daily as sometimes.
9.36.57: O gods, endowed with devotion, realise this and eschew your arrogance, worship me, the eternal Prakrti.
9.36.58: On hearing the merciful words of the goddess, the gods eulogised her, with their shoulders drooping with devotion.
9.36.59: O goddess of the universe, forgive us. O goddess, be pleased. O mother, let us not be arrogant again. Please be merciful.

9.36.60: O Brahmins, thus I have narrated to you the menifestation of Uma. By only hearing this men attain the great region.
9.36.61: O intelligent one, all of us are anxious to hear the episode of Durga every day. Please tell us another wonderful tale of the goddess.
9.36.7: O Suta, the most excellent of the story-tellers, we are not satiated even as we hear different nectarine stories narrated by you.
9.36.8: The most powerful son of Ruru, famous as Durgama secured the four Vedas as a result of the boon granted by Brahma.
9.36.9: Securing this strength that cannot be thwarted even by the gods he wrought havoc on the earth, making the gods tremble in heaven.
9.37.0: None offered charitable gifts; none performed penances; there was neither worship nor sacrifice. Then a great drought befell the earth extending to a period of a hundred years.
9.37.1: Rivers, oceans, tanks, wells and lakes dried. Trees and plants withered.
9.37.10: On seeing the misery of the distressed subjects the gods sought refuge in the Yogic Maya, Mahevari.
9.37.11: O Mahamaya, save all your people. Check your fury or the worlds will be ruined.
9.37.12: O ocean of mercy, O suppor tress of the distress¬ ed, kill this demon too just as you have killed Sumbha, Nisumbha. Dhumraksa, Canda, Muncjla, Raktabija, Madhu, Kaiabha and Mahisa.
9.37.13: Boys are guilty of offence at every step but who on earth brooks it except the mother?
9.37.14: When miseries afflict the gods and the brahmins you incarnate for the welfare of the people.
9.37.15: On hearing the distress of the gods the merciful goddess revealed to them her form possessed of many eyes.
9.37.16: The goddess w'ith her lotus-face beaming with delight held in her four hands the bow, the arrows, the lotus and different fruits and roots.
9.37.17: On seeing her people scorched and distressed, the goddess was dejected. With her eyes full of mercy she cried for nine days and nights.
9.37.18: The tears took the forms of thousands of water- currents released from her eyes. The worlds, the plants and medicinal herbs were delighted by them.
9.37.19: They turned into the rivers and oceans of deep waters. Vegetables, roots and fruits grew on the earth.
9.37.2: To the learned and the gods she distributed the
9.37.20: All including the gods, brahmins and men were satisiied. Then the goddess said — "What else shall I do for you?"
9.37.21: The gods then gathered together and said, "The people have been rendered happy and satisfied. O goddess, be pleased and redeem the Vedas taken by Durgama.'*
9.37.22: After saying "So be it" she said. "Go ye all to yotir abodes. Ere long I shall give you the Vedas."
9.37.23: Then the joyous gods returned to their abodes after
9.37.24: V Then a great bustle arose in the three regions heaven, earth and sky. On hearing it the son of Ruru besieged the city immediately.
9.37.25: Then after creating a big circle of splendour all round for the protection of the gods, Siva herself came out of it.
9.37.26: A great battle ensued between the goddess and the Daitya. Both showered arrows in the battle, piercing the armour of each other.
9.37.27: In the meantime ten beautiful forms came out of Kali Viz Tara, Ghinnamasta, Srividya, Bhuvanesvari, Bhairavi, Bagala, Dhumra, Srimattripurasundarl, Matahgi and Mahavidya with weapons in their hands.
9.37.28: Then appeared innumerable mothers of divine forms, wearing the digit of the moon and with a lustre resembling the splendour of lightning.
9.37.29: Then a terrible combat ensued between the Asuras and the mothers. The army of the son of Ruru, consisting of a hundred Aksauhinis was killed in the battle.
9.37.3: Then the goddess struck Durgama with the edge of her trident. He fell on the earth like an uprooted tree.
9.37.30: Thus after killing him the goddess redeemed the four Vedas and gave them to the gods.
9.37.31: O Ambika, for our welfare that form of infinite eyes was assumed by you. Hence sages will glorify you as!atak.s!.
9.37.32: Since the worlds were sustained by you with vege¬ tables sprouting from your body, you will be famous as Sakambharl.
9.37.33: O Siva, since you killed the Daitya Durgama you will be known as Durga.
9.37.34: O Yogic slumber, O Mahabala, O bestower of knowledge, O the mother of the universe, Obeisance be to you.
9.37.35: Obeisance to the heroine of infinite universes known as the supreme goddess in the Mahavakyas as Tat- tvamasi.
9.37.36: O Mother, we who are unaware ot your power and greatness, cannot adequately eulogise you who are inaccessi¬ ble through words, mind or body and whose eyes are the sun and the moon.
9.37.37: Who else will bestow mercy on seeing us the gods except the great goddess Sataksi the mother?
9.37.38: Effort shall be made by you so that the three worlds will not be pestered continuously with obstacles and our enemies shall be destroyed.
9.37.39: Just as the cows run about in excitement quickly on seeing their calves in distress, so also I, Sati, am excited on seeing you in distress and run about.
9.37.4: Even a moment appears to be a Yuga if I do not see you since I look at you as my own children for whom I am ready even to lay down my life.
9.37.40: No worry or anxious thought need be entertained by you endowed with devotion as long as I stand by you destroying your distress.
9.37.41: In the manner I have killed the Daiiyas I shall kill the Asuras. You need not entertain any doubt in this regard. Truth, I am speaking the truth.
9.37.42: I shall be born of the womb in the lamily of cowherds as the daughter of Yasoda wife of Nanda, when Sumbha and Nisumbha will be born as Daityas. I shall kill the demons and become famous. Men will therefore call me Nandaja.
9.37.43: Since I shall be taking the form of a bee and killing the demon Aruna, men will glorify me as Bhramari
9.37.44: Again I shall take a terrible form and devour the Raksasas. I shall then be famous as Bhima Devi.
9.37.45: The goddess Sataksi, Sakambhari and Durga are identical. In all the three the individual is the same.
9.37.46: O blessed disciple of Vyasa, O Suta the most excellent among the knowers of the Puranas, we wish to hear some other story of the lord.
9.37.47: We wish to hear the most excellent sacred rites of Uma, the mother of the universe, those which were narrated to Vyasa the great Atman by Sanatkumara
9.37.48: All of you are blessed great souls; steady in your devotional rites to the goddess. Now listen devotedly to the well-guarded secret of the great Sakti.
9.37.49: O omniscient Sanatkumara, O intelligent son of Brahma, I wish to hear the wonderful holy rites of Uma.
9.37.5: O Dvaipayana of great intellect, listen to the full description I am going to give of the secret that you ask.
9.37.50: Three paths of the glorious mother have been narrated which yield both worldly pleasures and salvation. They are paths of knowledge, holy rites and devotion.
9.37.51: O excellent sage, the chief reason of liberation is the Yoga. Kriyayoga is the greatest means of liberation.
9.37.52: One shall know the Maya as Pralqrti and the wielder of Maya as the eternal Brahman. After realising the identity of the two one is released from the world by bondage.
9.37.53: O Vyasa, listen to the merit of the person who builds a temple to the goddess either of stone or of wood or of mud. He who builds a temple to the goddess attains the benefit which a person who worships every day through Yoga attains in plenty. That virtuous soul who builds the temple for the glorious mother enables a thousand past and a thousand future members of his family to attain liberation.
9.37.54: The sins committed by a person in a crore of births, whether they be small or big, are quelled at the very moment when the foimdation for temple of the glorious mother is laid.
9.37.55: The glorious great Amba is the most excellent among all the deities just as Ganga and Sona among the rivers, the earth in forbearance, the ocean in majesty and the sun among the planets.
9.37.57: He who makes idols with the full complement of characteristics fearlessly attains indeed the great, region of Uma.
9.37.58: After installing the image of the goddess, in the auspicious stars, planets and the season, man becomes con¬ tented and blessed by the favour of the Yogamaya.
9.37.59: After installing an auspicious image of the goddess one can redeem the men of one's family both of the past and the future.
9.37.6: O leading sage, by installing the goddess the merit derived is a crorc times mare than that derived by establish¬ ing the three worlds.
9.37.7: The merit cannot be calculated of the man who instals the Pari caya tana®® deities with Ambika in the centre and the other four in the four quarters.
9.37.8: One attains great merit by repeating the names ofVisnu a crore times during the solar and lunar eclipses, a hundred crore times by repeating the names of Siva, a crore times by repeating the names of Sridevi, a crore times by building the palace for the goddess. To the man who instals the image of the goddess, mother of the universe, identical with the three Vedas there is nothing inaccessible, thanks to the merit of the glorious mother. His sons, grandsons and others flourish. All his sins perish.
9.37.9: Even those who desire mentally the installation of the excellent image attain the great region of Uma inaccessi¬ ble even to the sage.
9.38.0: Those who have resorted only to the goddess the cause of the universe, are not or4inary men. They are the Ganas of the Goddess herself.
9.38.1: Those who repeat the two syllables "U-ma" day and night, sitting, sleeping or moving become Siva's Ganas.

9.38.13: The goddess mother bestows her blessings on the family of the person who builds a beautiful temple for the goddess.
9.38.14: The glorious mother repeats day and night: "May my devotees live for a hundred years. Let them not be the victims of adversities."
9.38.15: Whatever an aspirant solicits after installing and worshipping the image of the goddess he attains that.
9.38.16: Who can calculate the merit of a person who performs the ablution of the installed image of the glorious mother, with clarified butter after smearing it with honey?
9.38.17: The devotee shall perform the ablution of the godd¬ ess either with water scented with sandal, aguru, camphor maihsi, musta etc. or with the milk of single-coloured cows.
9.38.18: The excellent offering shall be made with the incense of eighteen ingredients. The waving of the light for the goddess shall consist of wicks soaked in ghee or camphor.
9.38.19: On the fifth, eighth, ninth and tenth days of the dark lunar half and on new moon days the devotee shall worship the mother of the worlds with fragrant flowers.
9.38.2: Jananisukta, Srisukta or Devisukta shall be recited or Mulamantra shall be chanted.
9.38.20: All flowers except Visnukranta and Tulasi are pleasing to the goddess particularly the lotus.
9.38.21: He who offers golden or silver flowers to the god¬ dess goes to the greatest abode where crores of Siddhas live.
